question: After a cost review, a team switches every Claude task to the fastest and cheapest tier. What is the greatest risk?
options: A) Every task will now be completed rather faster than the team is able to review the output properly.
B) Responses will be much shorter, so colleagues will have to ask more follow-up questions.
C) The small number of genuinely hard analyses will thin out with no agreed standard to catch it.
D) The team will be unable to move any of the tasks back to a deeper tier at a later stage.
correct_answers: C) The small number of genuinely hard analyses will thin out with no agreed standard to catch it.
explanations: Incorrect. Faster turnaround is not the danger, and review capacity is a separate scheduling matter.
Incorrect. Length is set by what is asked for rather than by the tier, and it is not the substantive exposure.
Correct. A blanket switch removes reasoning depth from the work that needed it, and without a defined quality bar the degradation shows up as slightly weaker answers nobody flags.
Incorrect. Nothing prevents moving back; the tier can be changed whenever the team decides to.
